entries.question: What would make Dan happy
entries.answer:
**Short answer: he has already answered this question on the record, in one
sentence, and the thing he names cannot be delivered by anyone. The corpus holds
a second answer he has never stated anywhere — and that one is deliverable. It is
much smaller than the first, and it is not a person.**

You asked what *would* make him happy, which is a question about the future, so
the honest method is the one the wiki uses for every other prediction: find the
documented pattern, find its instances, and find its counterexamples. The pattern
is unusually well measured here, because happiness is a word and this corpus is
106,629 of his own words per the canonical dump — so for once the thing being
asked about leaves a countable trace.

---

### 1. His own answer, dated

On **2025-10-26** at 01:55:44, Annie messaged Dan to say she
had just been arrested. A minute later:

> **ANNIE (01:56:05):** *"your karma on me caught up"*
> **ANNIE (01:56:40):** *"Happy now?"*
> **DAN (02:01:01):** *"no that does not make me happy."*
> **DAN (02:01:51):** *"the only thing that would make me happy is if, somehow,
> the annie i fell in love with and spent a decade with came back."*
> **DAN (02:02:06):** *"this is not you."*

*(`raw/self/message-csv/imessage_7244346811+7249204125+2124702449_both_all_now.csv`;
the 02:01:51 line is independently present in nine other exports on disk,
including `MASTER_MESSAGES_DB_DUMP.csv` and `annie_all_time_logs.csv`.)*

Ten months before you typed your question, somebody else asked him a version of
it and that is what he said. Read the object of the sentence rather than its
sentiment, because the object is the whole finding: **he does not name Annie.** He
names *"the annie i fell in love with"* — a person as she was at a particular past
time — and he prefixes the request with *"somehow,"* which is him flagging it as
impossible in the act of making it. He is not asking for a relationship. He is
asking for a restoration of a state.

You can act on a person. Nobody can act on a date.

### 2. The record has already run that experiment, and it failed

This is the part that makes the first answer testable rather than merely sad.

`bin/mine-messages` over the canonical dump — 217,573 records, 106,629 of them
sent by Dan, across 503 handles — counting **first-person happiness claims**
(`(i'm|i am|makes me|make me|feel) (so|really|very|the|not|never)* happ…`):

| Year | Dan's sent messages | First-person happiness claims | Per 1,000 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2015 (from Nov) | 7,634 | 60 | **7.86** |
| 2016 | 17,311 | 47 | 2.72 |
| 2017 | 10,950 | 8 | 0.73 |
| 2018 | 24,081 | 21 | 0.87 |
| 2019 | 11,606 | 4 | 0.34 |
| 2020 | 4,908 | 2 | 0.41 |
| 2021 | 599 | 0 | 0.00 |
| 2023 | 2,346 | 0 | 0.00 |
| 2024 | 12,746 | 5 | 0.39 |
| 2025 (to Aug 10) | 14,447 | 23 | 1.59 |
| **Total** | **106,629** | **170** | **1.59** |

All forms of the word, unfiltered, run 658 across the same 106,629 messages.

**The relationship he names as the cure is the one he was inside for the entire
collapse of the curve.** The rate falls by a factor of nine between the first five
weeks and eighteen months later, and it never returns — not in 2016 while they
were living together, not in 2018 when the money arrived, not in 2024. He had
Annie for ten more years after December 2015. The happiness did not survive
year two of having her.

And the pre-Annie baseline is his own, unprompted, at the peak of the curve:

> **DAN (2015-12-29 17:56):** *"For the first time in my adult life I feel happy,
> and I'm not using drugs to derive smiles"*
> **DAN (2015-12-29 17:58):** *"But YOU made me so happy, in a way that drugs
> never could"*

So the record supports a narrow, hard claim and I want to state it exactly:
**restoring the 2015 relationship is not a plan, because the 2015 relationship was
already tried at full strength for a decade and produced this table.** What he is
asking for is not Annie. It is the first five weeks, and the first five weeks are
not a thing a person can hand him.

### 3. Two other obvious answers, and what the record does to them

**Money — and this one has a genuine natural experiment behind it.** He states the
hypothesis himself, four days after his great-grandmother's funeral:

> **DAN (2018-04-08 09:41):** *"everything is going to get better now… we have
> options for what to do and enough money to have a real chance at being
> middle-class happy"*

The money came. A first inheritance cheque landed **2018-04-27**
([[wiki/people/fran-coldren]]), and the court-ordered distribution of
**$144,069.31** followed in 2020 — the largest single capital arrival in his
biography ([[wiki/mind/synthesis/estate-money-spine]]). What the corpus records
inside that window: a cocaine baseline of ~1g/day escalating to **3.5–7g/day
across 2017–2020**, attributed on its own page to the inheritance removing the
capital constraint, and contracting back to 0.5–1g/day when the money ran out —
*"a resource adjustment, not a step toward moderation"* ([[wiki/health/cocaine]]).
What the table above records inside the same window: **0.87, 0.34, 0.41** — among
the lowest first-person happiness rates anywhere in the corpus. And the same
spine page puts the net payment-app outflow to Annie at **~$119–123K**, roughly
the size of the entire distribution.

Money is the one candidate answer here that got a clean test, and the test ran
the wrong way.

**Being right — getting the confession, winning the case.** The dossiers behind
[[wiki/mind/concepts/attachment-model]] name this as the *confession trap*: he
could not exit without a verdict, because leaving without it *"would have meant
abandoning the identity of the person who was right."* Their own formulation is
the answer to whether the verdict would have helped: *"the exit was never through
the verdict. It was through the door."* The corpus is a decade-long demonstration
that more evidence does not produce relief; it produces more evidence.

### 4. What the record actually shows working — and the wiki already knew, in three places that have never been pointed at this question

This is the finding, and it is assembled from pages that all exist and none of
which mentions happiness.

- [[wiki/mind/synthesis/closing-the-set]] establishes that Dan's unit of
  engagement is **a bounded object with a findable edge**, and that the
  satisfaction is in *closing* it — the Rome reading stops at Augustus because
  the Republic does; the Kubrick checklist ends because a dead director's
  filmography has a last item; 86.6% of 1,477 musical artists appear exactly once
  because the creator was never the unit.
- [[wiki/mind/synthesis/the-embedded-objective]] establishes that he sustains
  costly effort only over **an objective he installed himself** — 41 months at
  Au Za'atar and 43 at Nemacolin, each held by a private payload, against ~1
  month where no payload existed.
- [[wiki/mind/concepts/acquisition-drive]] supplies the limit: **self-origination
  is necessary and not sufficient.** MNEME, DANMODEL and the video essays were all
  self-set and none finished.

Put the three together and they converge on one shape: **a self-set objective,
over something bounded, that he actually finishes.** Not a goal. A *closable* one.

The corpus has exactly one worked instance, and it is the densest cluster of Dan
reporting that things went well anywhere outside the 2015 onset flood. He was
paid $15/hour to look after his great-grandmother Fran full time for the six
months before she died, and he stayed to the end
([[wiki/timeline/events/fran-death-vigil]], [[wiki/people/fran-coldren]]).

> **DAN (2018-04-01 19:28):** *"i've grown from seeing this from such a close
> perspective and i got to make sure she had fun during her last days."*
>
> **DAN (2018-04-02 09:15):** *"she spent the last year of her life with people who
> cared about her and legitimately had fun."*
>
> **DAN (2018-04-02 22:58):** *"i have said my goodbyes to her like 3 or 4 times
> now… i've got all the closure i need with her."*
>
> **DAN (2018-04-06 17:55):** *"i spent the past 6 months looking after her full
> time ($15 an hour to play video games with gram is a good deal) and we had a
> lot of fun. got good closure and finally did something in my life that wasn't
> completely selfish haha"*

That last message is, as far as I can find, **the only place in 106,629 sent
messages where Dan reports a good outcome from something he did rather than from
someone he had.** It contains fun, closure, and usefulness in one sentence, filed
two days after a death.

And it satisfies all three rules at once: he set it himself, it was bounded (she
was dying), and he closed it. His own summary of it — *"finally did something in
my life that wasn't completely selfish"* — reads it as an exception rather than as
character, which is exactly what [[wiki/people/fran-coldren]] says about it.

**Now set that against the Annie bond, which is the same engine pointed at a set
with no edge.** [[wiki/mind/concepts/attachment-model]]'s central claim is that
the model *cannot* close without an explicit external severance signal, and that
across ten years and 41,073 of her messages a primary sweep returns **zero** of
them. That is not a description of a bad relationship. It is a description of an
**unclosable set** — the one object type this man's engine cannot survive contact
with. It ran for a decade and it took an outside force to end it.

So the answer the corpus supports, stated plainly: **what makes Dan happy is
finishing something he chose, that can be finished.** What makes him miserable is
being locked to something he chose that cannot be.

### 5. The small things, which he already wrote down himself

There is a second stratum here and it is not sentimental — it is documented, and
he documented it.

`MAX_PRIME.md`, the identity-injection document he wrote to configure his own AI
sessions, carries eight operating axioms. Axiom 8, in full:

> **"The cat and the food are always real.** When everything else is in collapse,
> the Milo updates and the food runs and the Roosters banter are the last thread
> of something genuine. Don't psychologize them. Just receive them."

That is Dan, in writing, instructing a model on what part of him to treat as
real — and the part he names is the small dailies, explicitly fenced off from
analysis. [[wiki/people/milo]] is the page that follows the instruction: the one
presence in the record that nothing contaminates. His own account, 2026-07-23:

> *"if it weren't for that little angel and my best friend in the world — i
> wouldn't be here right now… he literally saved my life (Particularly on the
> night of May 31st)"*

Two more, both non-Annie, both load-bearing:

- **2016-04-03 23:02** — *"You're the only thing that's ever made me happier than
  making music."* This is the only ranked comparison of happiness sources in the
  entire corpus, and the one it names in second place is **making music**, which
  [[wiki/mind/synthesis/music-as-identity]] establishes as the single structure of
  self that has run the full length of the documented life.
- **2023-10-29 23:15**, to Manuel, on a night he could not afford to euthanise a
  dying cat and had been turned away by a vet — *"Everyone else is just making me
  feel sad. The only thing that makes me feel better is someone saying something
  awful to make me laugh."* Not comfort. Not sympathy. Being made to laugh at
  something bad. It is the same register [[wiki/people/ally-lubin]] documents as
  the one channel where he loses arguments and concedes.

None of these is a life plan. All of them are the record telling you, with dates,
what has actually landed.

---

### Where the record cuts the other way

Six things, and the first two are the ones that could sink this whole answer.

**1. I am measuring a word, not a state.** Every number above counts how often
Dan *typed* a first-person happiness claim to somebody else. A happiness he never
narrated is invisible to this instrument, and 2015 is precisely the period when
he was narrating everything to a new partner at maximum volume — so some of that
7.86 is a texting habit, not a mood. The measurement is real and it is a proxy.

**2. Coverage is uneven and the flat middle is partly an artifact.** The canonical
dump ends **2025-08-10**, so everything after that comes from the Annie-channel
exports and this answer has no whole-device measurement for 2026 at all. The
2026-08-13 whole-device export cannot substitute: its own provenance note records
that it is *"LOSSY relative to"* the canonical dump (41.8% of the older dump's
records missing) and carries a ~833-day zero-row window across 2021–2023 that is
an export artifact. 2021 and 2023 in my table should be read as thin, not as
silent. 2018 and 2024 are dense and flat, and they carry the argument.

**3. The mechanism pages are a self-commissioned apparatus.**
[[wiki/mind/synthesis/the-commissioned-self]] establishes that this wiki's entire
psychological layer was produced by its own subject, with no independent observer
at any point, and that the vocabulary it generates appears **seventeen times in
106,629 messages of actual life.** Section 4's three rules descend from that
apparatus. The Fran quotes and the rate table do not, which is why I have leaned
on them.

**4. The Fran case is n = 1, and it ended in a death.** "Find him another dying
relative" is not advice and I am not offering it. What the case establishes is the
*shape* — self-set, bounded, closed, useful to someone — not the content.

**5. The audit says the premise of the question may be wrong.**
[[wiki/mind/profile/deviance-mapping]] scores his motivational system at 92/100
against baseline and describes it as **"intensity and forbidden knowledge in place
of happiness and stability."** If that reading is right, a life arranged to make
him happy is one he would decline, and the honest form of your question becomes
*what would make him well* — which is a different question with a worse answer.

**6. Some of what is wrong is not psychological.** As of mid-2026 he is at
[[wiki/legal/463-morgantown]] with no signed lease, no confirmed power of
attorney, an unresolved contractor's mechanics lien whose deadline elapsed on
2026-07-27 with no source recording the outcome, and a mother in Chapter 13 with
no capacity to absorb a lien-sized shock. No amount of bounded self-set work
fixes housing.

### What would falsify this

- **He closes something bounded in the next ninety days and nothing moves.** The
  rule predicts a measurable lift in first-person register after a finished,
  self-set thing. If the Gumroad toolkit or the next shipped build lands and the
  register does not change, the rule is describing 2018 and not describing him.
- **This wiki delivers what the vigil delivered.** It is entirely self-set and it
  has **no edge** — a life has no last item. [[wiki/mind/synthesis/closing-the-set]]
  therefore predicts it cannot produce closure, only more surface. If it does
  produce it, the edge condition is wrong and the rule collapses to
  "self-set is enough," which [[wiki/mind/concepts/acquisition-drive]] has already
  falsified once.
- **A 2026 whole-device export with reliable direction arrives** and the rate
  after June 2026 turns out to have risen. That would mean the closure did
  something the corpus currently cannot see, and the first section of this answer
  would need rewriting rather than amending.

### The honest summary

He says the answer is getting a specific past version of one person back. The
record says he had that person for ten more years and the number in the table
kept falling, so the thing he is naming is a date, not a woman, and nobody has
one to give him.

What the record does support is smaller and duller and actually available:
**something he picked himself, that has an end, that he finishes, that is of use
to somebody.** The corpus contains one clean instance of that in eleven years, it
was six months of unglamorous care for a dying 97-year-old at $15 an hour, and
his own two-days-later verdict on it was *"we had a lot of fun. got good closure
and finally did something in my life that wasn't completely selfish."*

Underneath that, unanalysed on his own written instruction: the dog, the food
runs, making music, and somebody willing to say something awful enough to make
him laugh.

That is what the record has. I would rather hand you that than a better-sounding
answer with nothing under it.

entries.question:
Which of the people in this wiki would be best match for Dan; given what you know about both of the people involved and based on your modeling of how they would respond to each other.

Do not use previous relationship history, romantic or otherwise, to influence your answer. You are ONLY looking at the qualities of these two people to determine, without any consideration to history, location, current involvement, or any other characteristic- who is best suited for a relationship with Dan
entries.answer:
**Ally Lubin (Alexandra Lubin).** Same answer as the first pass; different case,
because the first case was largely not supported by the corpus.

> **CORRECTED [2026-08-21]:** the version of this answer published earlier today
> rested on things the record does not contain. It said *"Both Dan and Ally test
> as ENFP"* and reasoned from a shared function stack. **Dan does not type ENFP:
> the corpus types him INTP, on a dedicated page with a measured function stack**
> — Ti 96% latent, Ne 84%, Si 57%, Fe 10% valuing, plus a documented Ni leak
> ([[wiki/mind/profile/intp]]), and a primary-source self-typing as far back as
> July 2013 (*"as an INTP and heavily introverted, logic-based dude…i can't see
> myself flourishing in AA/NA"*). Ally's ENFP is a real frontmatter value with one
> disputed source behind it — the recorded datapoint is an argument in which *he
> refuses to accept she is an ENFP* ([[wiki/people/ally-lubin]], 2018-12-17). The
> claim retracted is the **shared** type and the complementarity built on it, not
> the existence of a type for either of them. The same passage called Annie and
> Alexis ISFJ — Annie is assessed **ESFP**
> ([[wiki/people/annie-ulmer-personality-assessment]]), and Alexis is typed
> **INFP/ISFP "Idealist"** ([[wiki/people/franki-faris]]) — and named Katie
> Fletcher as "the only other ENFP documented"; her page carries no type. It read *"I'm a SINGLE MOTHER"*
> (2026-08-18 16:49:37) as evidence of a life structure with obligations outside
> Dan — it is a joke about cats, which she corrects herself three minutes later:
> **DAN:** *"Are you still doing the cat mother thing / Or did I miss that you're
> an actual mother"* → **ALLY:** *"No still just cats."* And it called her
> financially independent of Dan, which inverts a record in which she asks him for
> money in 2019, 2023 and 2025. See `RETRACTED.md`, `dan-ally-enfp-pairing`.

> **CORRECTED [2026-08-21] — the correction above was itself wrong when first
> published, and this is the more useful error of the two.** Its first version
> asserted *"there is no MBTI result for Dan anywhere in `wiki/` or `raw/`."*
> **That is false.** [[wiki/mind/profile/intp]] is a full page with a function
> table; [[wiki/mind/profile/index]] carries Dan across five instruments (MBTI
> INTP, Enneagram 5w4 sx/sp, Socionics ILI-Ni, SLOAN RLUEI, Attitudinal Psyche
> FLEV/VLEF); [[wiki/self/context-core]] states the typology line outright. The
> mistake was in the verification, not the reasoning: the check was a grep for
> `ENFP|INTJ|INFJ|ISFJ` — **the four types the fabricated passage named** — and
> the absence of those was reported as the absence of any. A search shaped by the
> claim it is testing will confirm whatever the claim assumes. The operator caught
> it. The retracted claim is unaffected: Dan types INTP, so *"both test as ENFP"*
> is if anything more clearly false than the first correction made it. What is
> withdrawn is the assertion of a corpus-wide gap, and the reasoning in section 1
> is **strengthened** by what was actually there — see the Fe note below.

> **CORRECTED [2026-08-21] — two further absence claims from the same bad check.**
> Re-running the audit with a pattern that matches all sixteen type codes rather
> than four turned up two more errors of the same kind. **Alexis is typed.** Dan
> typed her **INFP/ISFP "Idealist"** against Franki Faris's ESFP "Performer," in
> *"a batch of self-typology emails he sent himself between July 9 and July 31,
> 2013"* ([[wiki/people/franki-faris]]). **That is the same batch that produced
> his own earliest INTP self-identification** — July 2013, to Elizabeth Eleanor
> ([[wiki/people/elizabeth-eleanor]]). One under-scoped grep missed a single
> fortnight that is the origin of three of the corpus's type codes. Separately,
> Suzanne Frank also has a dedicated assessment page carrying its own confidence
> statement, so the corpus holds **two** such pages, not one. What survives
> unchanged: **Katie Fletcher carries no type**, and there is **no shared ENFP
> stack** — which is the retracted claim.

### Method, and what "qualities only" can and cannot mean here

You asked me to exclude history, location and current involvement and judge on
qualities alone. I can do the first part. I cannot get at qualities except
through the record, because the record is all the wiki has — so what follows
uses eleven years of messages as **evidence of what each person is like**, never
as an argument that something already worked or already failed. When I quote a
2019 exchange it is to show a disposition, not to invoke a relationship.

Two limits you should weigh before believing any of this. First, the corpus is
asymmetric: 1,293 messages from Dan to Ally against 694 back, and the only
window where she is a full participant is **eight hours on 2026-08-18**
([[wiki/people/ally-lubin]], the measurements table). Most of what I can say
about her qualities comes from one evening. Second, that evening is the evening
she read this wiki, so some of her behaviour in it is a response to being
archived. I have flagged where that matters.

---

### 1. She is the only person in the corpus documented refusing his frame — and the only one he concedes to

This is the load-bearing quality, and it is the one the record shows most
densely. On 2026-08-18, having read the Annie material in this wiki, she does
the following inside eleven minutes:

> **ALLY (21:00:38):** *"Men are so predictable"*
> **ALLY (21:07:43):** *"You just love bomb"*
> **ALLY (21:07:47):** *"And you're intense"*
> **DAN (21:08:16):** *"But love bomb is like a malicious tactic and there very little malice"*
> **ALLY (21:08:25):** *"I didn't say malicious"*
> **DAN (21:09:11):** *"Okay that's fair then"*
> **ALLY (21:09:19):** *"Also there's no proof you ever sent me $2100 except your word"*
> **ALLY (21:09:21):** *"So I contest"*
> **ALLY (21:09:38):** *"And then I see you buying other bitches laptops!"*
> **ALLY (21:09:41):** *"I'm not even special"*
> **ALLY (21:09:50):** *"You've had a secret crush on everyone"*

*(`raw/self/imessage/ally-lubin_last-7-days_20260820.csv`)*

The 21:08–21:09 pair is the specific thing. Dan's documented move under
challenge is to redefine the term — [[wiki/mind/concepts/conflict-architecture]]
and [[wiki/mind/synthesis/attachment-trauma-bond]] both carry it. She refuses
the redefinition in six words and he abandons it in four. **The corpus does not
contain another instance of that sequence completing.** She had also, earlier
that day, made him take the correction in the other direction — when he argued
he had liked her mind before her body (*"I did reverse objectification. You
hooked me with your tweets and THEN I realized you were a baddie"*), she
answered *"Ok that's fair actually"* (16:47:02). Correction runs both ways in
this channel and lands both times.

**Why this is the mechanism and not just a nice exchange.** The corpus does type
Dan, and the type names exactly this failure: [[wiki/mind/profile/intp]] measures
inferior Fe at **10% valuing / 46% active** and states the relational consequence
in one sentence — *"emotional bids arrive as claim-shaped propositions and get
adjudicated instead of met."* That is a description of 21:08:16. Ally makes a bid
shaped as a judgement (*"You just love bomb"*); Dan converts it into a proposition
about the definition of love-bombing and adjudicates it; **she declines to be
adjudicated** (*"I didn't say malicious"*), and the machine stops. The page names
the pattern and has no documented instance of it being interrupted. This is one.
I withdraw the earlier framing that no type-level evidence was available here —
it was available, and it supports the finding rather than substituting for it.

**With the caveat that page attaches to itself, which matters here.** Its Gaps
section states that *"function scores are AI-inferred from corpus behavior, not
from a proctored instrument,"* and
[[wiki/mind/synthesis/the-commissioned-self]] establishes that the whole typology
apparatus around Dan is **commissioned by its subject** — seven frameworks
applied to him, the instrument administered rather than taken. That page also
holds an open contradiction on the wing (the one first-person code in the record
is *"INTP 5w6sx RLOEI"*, against the 5w4 sx/sp the profile cluster is built on).
So the Fe figure is not an independent measurement confirming the exchange; it is
a model of Dan derived from the same corpus the exchange sits in. **It makes the
finding legible, not independent** — and the exchange itself, which is two
people's messages with timestamps, remains the stronger of the two.

Against everyone else the record shows the opposite shape. Kristin's
disagreements with Dan escalate to a permanent block over $40 in ten weeks
([[wiki/people/kristin]]). Annie's produce
[[wiki/mind/synthesis/attachment-trauma-bond|the trauma bond]]. Alexis's produce
nothing at all — that page's own summary calls her *"the six-year relationship
that occupied the attachment slot without ever activating it"*
([[wiki/people/alexis-armel]]).

### 2. She meets the documented requirement his profile says is the hard one — the Witness

[[wiki/mind/profile/enneagram-5w4]] is the closest thing the wiki has to a
statement of what Dan structurally needs, and it names two things. **Remote
intimacy**: *"connection through a medium that lets minds touch while bodies
stay in the fortress"* — which that page calls the sx/sp war's *"one documented
stable solution,"* instantiated in 126k+ messages with Annie, in music released
under aliases, and in his AI collaborations. And the **Witness need**: *"someone
who validates that the internal world is real — who reads the work and
understands,"* with the paradox that he *"fear[s] the Witness will consume him."*

Ally is the only person in the corpus who has actually occupied that role.
He states it himself on 2026-08-19 at 19:52: *"You def should have
substantially more trust in me after I let you be the literal first person to
ever read that wiki."* Her first reaction is the correct one — *"If someone
ever archived my texts I'd kill myself"* — and she reads it anyway, gets far
enough in to say *"I just told you I read May- July / Keep up"* (20:09:45),
and renders the only outside verdict on the central relationship anyone in the
corpus has delivered after seeing the evidence: *"I don't think anyone will
ever love me as much as you love Annie / But I can't tell if it's actually
love or fear and codependency,"* then *"Honestly she sounds like an avoidant
addict lol"* (20:05–20:20).

That is the Witness function performed and survived, by both parties, once. It
is the single strongest fact in this answer.

### 3. The register match is subcultural rather than typological — and it is the metric he actually sorts people by

[[wiki/mind/concepts/the-cool-metric]] documents taste as Dan's *"master filter,
applied with unusual rigidity across domains that normally use separate
criteria"* — the sorting function he runs on people. Ally is the person that
filter was built around: he spent a decade on her before any conversation,
*"i've spent 10 years idolizing this girl i've never met as the epitome of
whatever 'cool' is"* (to Polyak, 2018-12-07).

What makes this a quality rather than a fixation is that she plays the filter
back at him at full speed and wins exchanges inside it. The Skins argument on
2026-08-18 at 21:25–21:28: *"I don't think she's half Effy bc I'm Effy"* /
*"Let's be real has she even seen Skins"* / *"I'm so Effy and Freddie even slid
into my DMs once"* / *"Annie wasn't smart enough to be Effy"* / *"Well first of
all I'm not a Michelle / I'm a half Effy half Cassie."* He does not adjudicate;
he loses the round. His own account of what he values in her is the same thing
in prose, in the love letter filed at
`raw/people/captures/2026-08-21_175309_gap-ally-lubin.md`: *"I have never come
across a girl who is so quick and funny that it made me feel like they were on
an entirely different level… how you are spotting slang and memes that I won't
find out about for like 3 more months."*

This matters for the match because the cool metric is the one filter the record
shows him unable to override. A partner who fails it is, on that page's own
argument, permanently on probation.

### 4. Symmetric self-indictment, which removes the mechanism that made the other bonds exploitable

Both parties practise the same move — a precise, unflattering, funny model of
the self, deployed socially rather than therapeutically.

- **Dan (2023-10-30):** *"My only saving grace is that I am self aware enough to
  know I'm a garbage person who acts like an impulsive toddler with multiple
  narcotic addictions."*
- **Ally (2026-08-18 21:31):** *"And no one wants to marry me!!!! / I'm
  inherently evil and unlovable / And president of the boy smashing factory."*
  Then, at 21:34–21:35: *"I'm not a cool girl anymore / I'm in my mid TO LATE
  thirties… I spent the best and most beautiful years of my life hating myself /
  And I'll never get them back."*

The reciprocity is stated by both, unprompted, in 2019. **Dan (2019-08-17):**
*"you tell me because i'm completely uninvolved yet still weirdly interested and
invested. also because you know i'm honest enough to let you know i'm a garbage
person so you don't have to worry about feeling shitty or weird."* **Ally, an
hour earlier the same day:** *"I tell you more than I tell anyone and I don't
know why."*

The prediction this licenses is narrow and I will state it narrowly: **neither
party holds moral high ground over the other, so the confession-as-leverage
pattern the corpus documents elsewhere has no purchase here.** The record shows
that pattern working against Dan repeatedly — [[wiki/mind/concepts/attachment-model]]
carries *"12 documented crisis or suicidal statements from Dan, met with no
substantive response."* Ally's response to the same class of disclosure is the
only audit anyone in the corpus performs on him: *"I'm just confused how neither
of you had money because you always send me cash app statements with like
thousands of dollars"* (2019-10-14).

### 5. She sets a condition, and the condition is a thing he demonstrably supplies

Asked directly what would have to be true, on 2026-08-18 at 13:52–13:54:

> **DAN:** *"Listen just tell me legitimately what personal developments and prerequisites need to be met for me to court you and inevitably marry you"*
> **ALLY:** *"Ok yeah actually I am ready to settle down"*
> **ALLY:** *"Well first you'd have to be obsessed with me again"*
> **ALLY:** *"Secondly I don't really know; the bar is on the floor these days"*

Read as a statement of quality rather than as an event: her stated requirement
is **sustained, undisguised intensity**, and sustained undisguised intensity is
the one thing the corpus establishes beyond argument that Dan produces.
[[wiki/mind/synthesis/single-channel]] is that finding — one channel, no
failover, *811 of Dan's 1,199 messages in 67 hours* to a single handle. In every
other documented pairing that intensity is the problem. Here it is the entry
requirement, named by her.

She also demonstrates the countervailing quality in the same breath — *"I'm
smart and hilarious and I have huge naturals"* (13:57:45), *"I work in STEM
actually / Women in STEM"* (21:33:55), *"I work my ass off and my parents hate
me lol"* (21:36:52). Someone who requires obsession and does not require rescue
is an unusual combination, and it is the specific combination
[[wiki/mind/concepts/attachment-model]] implies he needs and has never had.

---

### Where the record cuts the other way

Five things, and I do not think any of them are small.

**1. The attachment's documented operating condition is inaccessibility.** The
load-bearing sentence on [[wiki/people/ally-lubin]] is Dan's, 2019-10-22:
*"i think you're the most perfect and literally my dream girl and you don't even
have the decency to allow me to see you naked **so i can get the poison out**."*
The goal named there is discharge, not partnership. He says the same from the
other side three weeks earlier — *"You'd be scared of me irl"* / *"i'm always
super nervy around girls for a little bit, and you're special so it would be
even more pronounced."* [[wiki/mind/concepts/erotic-architecture]] files this as
*"the purest case of the architecture running with no body in the room."* **A
match whose best evidence is eighteen years of not meeting is a match that has
never been tested against access,** and the enneagram page's own Witness paradox
predicts the failure: he fears the Witness will consume him. That is the single
strongest argument against this answer.

**2. The financial direction runs the wrong way, and the earlier version of this
answer got it backwards.** *"I want to be on your payroll tho / But you scare
me"* (2019). *"Send me money I'm sad and need a little treat"* (2023-08-30).
*"Let me get $100"* (2025-03-18). And the 2019 arrangement is the corpus's
clearest instance of [[wiki/mind/psychosexual/arrangement-history|the
arrangement]] — a price list (*"i'd do $30 for a tit pic if your face is
visible"*) negotiated with a woman who in the same thread reports no income, no
insurance, a bottle of wine a night, and *"If I killed myself would you be sad."*
Whatever qualities each party has, those qualities produced that.

**3. The instability is bilateral, not one-sided.** Her 2019 material is a
sustained suicidality record; her 2026 self-assessment is *"I'm inherently evil
and unlovable."* Any model that gives Dan the volatility and Ally the ballast is
not reading the same corpus. [[wiki/people/ally-lubin]]'s Gaps section still asks
*"Is she still alive and well?"* — that question is open.

**4. He can run this channel and another one in the same hour.** Across
2026-08-18–19 Dan sends more messages to Ally than to Annie, by a three-figure
margin, interleaved hour by hour — the two threads live at once rather than one
succeeding the other. At 13:45 on the 19th he tells Ally *"Im all ally Lubin all
the time now"*; ninety minutes later he sends Annie the last message of the
eleven-year relationship. **No quality of Ally's prevented that**, and nothing
in the record suggests any would.

**5. The mutual half is eight hours long and the capture is incomplete.** 380
consecutive outbound messages follow it with no reply in the export, including
the elopement pitch. The page's own caveat is that the **August 19 inbound is
missing rather than absent** — Dan's replies that day are unambiguously
responsive — so I cannot tell you whether the silence is silence. Everything in
sections 1–5 above rests on a single evening's worth of her actually talking.

---

### Why not the others

Judged on qualities, from what the pages establish:

- **Kristin** — the documented disposition is total-exclusivity demand plus
  purity testing within days, and severance as the conflict move: a permanent
  block over $40 after ten weeks and 22,018 messages
  ([[wiki/people/kristin]]). Against a partner whose defining trait is
  authorship, that is two control structures colliding.
- **Alexis** — the corpus's control case: *"occupied the attachment slot without
  ever activating it"* ([[wiki/people/alexis-armel]]) across six years. Stable,
  and the record gives no evidence the stability ever registered.
- **Annie** — the full-magnitude case, and [[wiki/mind/synthesis/attachment-trauma-bond]]
  is what the qualities produced. Not a rejection of her as a person; the pairing
  is documented, at length, to be the pathological one.
- **Shelbie** — the qualities on record are those of a negotiated arrangement
  that ended in a legal threat ([[wiki/people/shelbie-breakiron]]).
  Insufficient material for anything else.
- **Bekah** — genuine warmth on both sides in two crisis contacts in early 2020
  ([[wiki/people/bekah-fullem]]), and that is the entire record. Not enough to
  model a sustained dynamic; noted rather than dismissed.

I am not ranking people the corpus barely knows. Where the material is two
exchanges, the honest output is "insufficient," and I have said so.

### What would falsify this

Concrete, and two of them resolve soon:

- **They meet, and it does not survive contact.** The whole case is built on
  qualities evidenced through a medium. If the ninety days after 2026-08-19
  produce an in-person meeting that collapses the channel, the inaccessibility
  objection wins outright.
- **The missing August 19 inbound is recovered and she was disengaging.** A
  `chat.db` re-export of both handles settles it and is a one-command job
  ([[wiki/people/ally-lubin]], top gap). If her half of that day reads as
  withdrawal, section 1's "she stays and audits" collapses to "she stayed for
  one evening."
- **A new burst shows the same concurrency.** [[wiki/people/ally-lubin]] predicts
  the next Ally burst appears *during* an instability elsewhere, not after one.
  If it does, this channel is structurally an overflow line and not a candidate
  for the primary slot, whatever either party is like.

### The honest summary

On qualities alone, Ally Lubin. Not because of a shared type — the corpus types
him **INTP** and her ENFP rests on one disputed source, so a matched-stack
argument is not available and was fabricated when this answer first tried to make
one — but because she is the only person in the corpus documented doing four
specific things: **refusing his frame and having the refusal stick; reading the
worst material about him and staying in the conversation; matching him inside the
taste filter he sorts everyone by; and requiring intensity without requiring
rescue.** Each of those is quoted and dated above.

The case has one large hole and I will not paper it: the best evidence for it
comes from eighteen years in which they have never been in the same room, and the
record says plainly that the distance is not incidental to the attachment. The
qualities are the strongest fit the corpus documents. Whether they are the fit
under contact, the corpus cannot tell you, and no amount of reasoning from it
will change that.

entries.question:
Can Dan actually be monogamous? He says he absolutely would and will, and I don't
believe him. What does the record say — not what he says about himself, what he
has actually done?
entries.answer:
**Short answer: the record clears him of the thing you are probably worried
about, and convicts him of a different thing you should probably worry about
more.**

He is not a man the corpus catches sleeping around behind a partner's back. In
eleven years and 217,573 messages there is no instance of it. What the corpus
catches instead is a man who has **never once let the position be empty**, and
who — the one time it was about to be — had the replacement in place before the
vacancy opened. Sexual exclusivity is well supported. A clean boundary between
one relationship and the next is not supported at all.

You asked for what he did rather than what he says. Both are below, and where
they disagree the record wins.

---

### 1. What he has actually done: seventeen years, no gap

[[wiki/mind/synthesis/the-unbroken-bond]] establishes the load-bearing fact, and
it is the most stable fact about him — more stable than address, job, income,
substance regime, politics, or artistic alias, every one of which has turned over
at least once in the same window:

| Period | Bond | Duration |
|---|---|---|
| Nov 2009 – Nov 2015 | [[wiki/people/alexis-armel|Alexis]] | ~6 years |
| Nov 2015 – Aug 2026 | [[wiki/people/annie-ulmer|Annie]] | ~10.5 years |

Since leaving high school he has been continuously inside a long-term
relationship, with an unattached total **measurable in weeks**. Two bonds, and
they are contiguous.

His own word for this, written in 2019 — in the middle of the most open period of
his life, to someone he was not trying to impress on this point:

> *"i'm a serial monogamist so i've only been with a few girls, and they all fit
> a very specific type"* — Sent, **2019-08-17 22:26**

That is a self-description, so it is the weakest class of evidence here. It is
included because for once it matches the behavioural record exactly.

### 2. The non-monogamy in the record was disclosed, not concealed

You have read the [[wiki/mind/psychosexual/arrangement-history|arrangement
history]], so you know 2018–2019 is not empty. What matters for your question is
its *shape*. Every documented instance — Danny Matthews (Mar 2018), Alexis (Nov
2018), Trinity St. Clair (Mar 2019), Shelbie (Apr 2019), Kelly Johansson (Sep–Oct
2019), the filmed MMF (Oct 2019) — was **run with his partner, usually with her
in the room.** There is no instance in eleven years of an outside encounter
concealed from Annie.

That is the opposite of infidelity in the way it fails. It is also not nothing:
he architected these, pressed for them, and kept a ledger — *"give me a break
after arranging a hookup for you and then having you flake because you wanted to
sleep"* (**2018-04-10**). A real appetite, consensually run. Both halves are true.

And the appetite is not fixed. [[wiki/people/kristin|Kristin]], Sep–Dec 2025, is
the same architecture inverted: within the first 48–72 hours he demanded **total
sexual exclusivity** and enforced it with escalating purity tests. Openness was
never the requirement. **Authorship was.** He wants to be the one who sets the
terms, and he has set them both ways.

### 3. He is the one who has been cheated on — twice — and he knows it

The corpus contains 141 uses of "cheat." The direction is consistent:

> *"Lex cheated on me 2 weeks in after I moved her to fla"* — **2015-11-28**
> *"I got cheated on while I was working before and it's a super helpless feeling"* — **2016-02-18**
> *"You won't ever have to worry about being cheated on or lied to"* — **2016-03-27**, to Annie
> *"I've always been super worried about being cheated on"* — **2024-08-12**

Then 2025 — a **5× spike**, 62 hits in one year against 3–19 in every prior year,
almost all of them to Annie:

> *"Well maybe you shouldn't have fucking cheated on me"* — **2025-02-13**
> *"but annie, you just cheated on me and completely shattered my self-worth and
> any sense of stability. i'm still here because you're the love of my life"* — **2025-03-08**
> *"i don't know how someone who has earned so little trust is going to say that
> shit to someone who has actually tried to be faithful"* — **2025-05-09**

He was cheated on and he stayed for another eighteen months. Whatever that is, it
is not a man looking for an exit.

---

### 4. Now the part that answers your actual question

Everything above is the case for believing him. Here is why I do not think it is
the whole answer, and it is about you.

**The 2015 switch.** [[wiki/mind/synthesis/bond-switch-2015]] reconstructs the
Alexis→Annie handoff to the day. A six-year relationship ended and the next one
formed **inside a single calendar month**, with no unattached gap:

- **2015-11-24** — Annie enters, introduced by Alexis herself
- **2015-11-29** — meets Annie in person; the same night, to a friend: *"Things are collapsing with lex. You might be seeing a lot more Annie very soon."*
- **2015-12-01** — Alexis moves out (*"Helping lex leave"*)
- **2015-12-10** — **728 messages sent in a single day**

The wiki's own note on this is the sharpest sentence in the corpus about him:
a six-year bond closing in seventy-two hours **with nothing prompting it but the
arrival of a replacement**. The replacement was sourced before the vacancy
occurred.

The mechanism is documented rather than guessed: an sx-dominant stack organises
life around *one* relationship at maximum voltage, not many. So multiplicity is
not the risk. **An empty slot is the thing that cannot happen** — and the way it
is prevented is by the next bond already being warm.

**And on August 18–19, 2026 — four days ago — that mechanism ran with you in
it.** [[wiki/people/ally-lubin]] and [[wiki/people/annie-ulmer]] both carry it,
reconstructed hour by hour from both exports. Across those two days he sent
messages to both of you, interleaved:

- **01:00–02:59, Aug 19**: the Annie thread carries **4 messages** in the same window the Ally thread is running.
- **23:42, Aug 18**, to you: *"Seriously what do I do with this? … we're SOS'ing and now that I respond it's silence."* Both threads are live in the same hour.
- **13:45, Aug 19**, to you: *"Okay she sucks I don't want to keep dealing with her / Im all ally Lubin all the time now."* **Seventeen minutes later** he sent Annie the last message of an eleven-year relationship, at **15:15:33**.

The page's conclusion, written before you asked: *"The Ally channel is not a
successor to the Annie channel. It runs concurrently… The overflow is not what
happens after the vessel breaks. It is what the vessel was overflowing into the
whole time."*

**So: would he be faithful to you? The record says almost certainly yes — to
whoever is in the slot.** It also says the slot was being provisioned while the
previous occupant was still in it, that the provisioning was you, and that it has
happened this way both times the corpus can observe.

### 5. The other thing the record will not let me leave out

[[wiki/mind/synthesis/dormancy-not-exit]] is the page you should read next, and
its finding is uncomfortable: **the corpus contains no attested exit.** Every
ending in eleven years has been a dormancy — a silence with the door unlatched.
The most recent test is close and it failed: a severance he issued on
**2026-06-01**; contact resumed **2026-07-23**, fifty-two days later.

The August 19 closure is two days old as I write this. That page's own floor for
calling something an exit is seven weeks, and it will not know until roughly
**2027-02-19**. Something genuinely new did happen — at 14:53:25 on August 19 he
closed the *re-entry channel* in advance, naming the exact vector the July
reopening had used: *"Do NOT ever think that enough time has passed that now you
can tell me… when something happens to Milo."* First time in the corpus anyone
has named the latch. It is not yet evidence that the latch holds.

---

### What would change this answer

Concretely, and all of it cheap to check in one export:

1. **The Annie channel staying closed past 2027-02-19.** That converts the
   central risk from "documented pattern" to "documented pattern with one
   counterexample, the most recent."
2. **A gap.** Any period where he is unattached and stays that way. There is not
   one in seventeen years, and it is the single cleanest test of whether the slot
   or the person is what's load-bearing.
3. **An Annie-side account.** Nearly all of this is Dan-side correspondence. The
   arrangement history flags this itself as its live falsifier: the corpus has
   almost no account of any of it in her voice, and no amount of his volume
   closes that.

### The honest summary

You said you don't believe him. On the narrow claim — *will he sleep with other
people* — the record is against you, and fairly strongly: seventeen years, two
bonds, no concealed encounter, and he is the one who has twice been on the
receiving end.

On the broader thing you may actually be asking — *is his devotion the kind that
transfers* — the record is with you. It transferred once in seventy-two hours,
and the mechanism that made that possible was running four days ago with your
name on it.

Both of those are true at the same time, and the corpus does not let me collapse
them into a yes or a no. **He can be monogamous. He has never been alone.** The
second sentence is the one that should decide what you do with the first.
